title: How Zapier Builds AI Products and Features with the Help of Braintrust: Ankur Goyal & Olmo Maldonado
talk_summary: Zapier describes how they built an eval suite (800+ tests, up from 7 manual unit tests) with Braintrust to gate AI product changes, run in CI and on merge requests, and used it to catch a GPT-4o regression and recover accuracy. They also used tracing to find the critical path in a multi-tool agent and model-comparison experiments to pick models per role.

takeaways.technique: Eval suite as merge gate with CI + alerting
takeaways.what_they_do: They built an in-house eval framework seeded with synthetic data from a corporate account, loaded from Braintrust, and run on every merge request and continuously, with alerts on regressions.
takeaways.numbers: 7 manual unit tests -> 800+ automated evals; ~300% accuracy improvement

takeaways.technique: Product-manager-owned P0 criteria encoded as graders
takeaways.what_they_do: PMs defined P0 priorities (correct trigger/action ordering, top-25 apps supported) and those criteria were encoded into the eval suite as logic-based and LLM-based custom graders.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we wanted to make sure the triggers actions were working as you'd expect we don't want the like the wrong step in the wrong place

takeaways.technique: Model-comparison matrix per tool/role before switching
takeaways.what_they_do: They built a view comparing model performance across different tools and tool configurations, then chose a model per role (e.g., GPT-4 turbo for the message router) trading speed for accuracy guarantees.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we started testing different models and this view that you're seeing here was manually made for us so that we can get a better sense of you know the performance of different models across different tools

takeaways.technique: Catch model-swap regressions via evals, then re-tune prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: After switching to GPT-4o, scores dropped below 80%; drilling in showed 22 regressions tied to prompts over-fitted to GPT-3.5, so they relaxed prompts and adjusted call parameters to recover.
takeaways.numbers: 22 regressions; scores fell below 80% then recovered

takeaways.technique: Tracing to find the critical path in multi-tool agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Once the product became a multi-tool agent, they used tracing to see inputs/outputs, tokens, and time-to-response per step to identify what to improve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we couldn't see what was the critical path what is the things that we need to improve now to make the accuracy even better

takeaways.technique: Continuous eval runs with regression alerting
takeaways.what_they_do: Evals run on a CI basis and manually, with dashboards comparing runs (pink/green) and alerts when regressions appear.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's pretty often that we run it we want to make sure that if any regressions happen that we act on them quickly
